years.theme: AI-Native Healthcare and Specialized Medical Devices

awards.project: Intelligent real-time patient monitoring and alert system built around a comprehensive camera dashboard and integrated data systems, designed to optimize the efficiency and responsiveness of hospital nursing staff.
A personalized advisor that matches SaaS startups to investors based on due-diligence-level data, making the screening process more efficient.
A technology that merges the worlds of board games and video games to create a new immersive sensory experience.
A portable nasometry device for clinicians to measure hypernasality in children with cleft palate, post-surgery.
An emergency cervical collar that protects the cervical spine without compressing the jugular veins.
An ML-powered electrotherapy device for stroke survivors that uses surface EMG to drive personalized rehabilitation.
Contact-free thermal and optical vital-sign monitoring for senior-care facilities.

years.theme: AI Safety, Additive Manufacturing, and B2B Marketplaces
years.scale_note: 56 competition concepts narrowed to 33 Demo Day projects; participation grew >25% over the previous year

awards.project: The first driver-conscious AI safety system to detect fatigue and distraction. Targets vehicle fleets with high operator liability (e.g., trucking).
awards.follow_on: Won 2024 UCI Stella Zhang New Venture Competition Grand Finale ($20K + $10K track) and placed 2nd in C&C Innovative Solutions SoCal Super Pitch. Now commercialized as Spotter AI's Sentinel platform at sentinel.spotter.ai - all-in-one fleet safety platform with real-time driver monitoring, DOT compliance alerts, and AI-powered hiring/screening. Spotter AI CEO/Co-Founder: Peidi Wu; Co-Founder, CTO and President: Gabriel Stonys.

awards.project: An autonomous bioinformatics analysis platform that runs single-cell RNA pipelines without manual setup. Uses Large Language Models for scRNA code generation and analysis ('the autonomous bioinformatician').
awards.follow_on: Won 1st place + $10,000 in the Stella Zhang NVC 2024 Life Science track. Co-founder Shushrruth Sai Srinivasan is a PhD student in CS at UCI; presented at the 2025 Health Care Forecast Conference.

awards.project: A maid- and household-help-matching platform tailored to the Indonesian market.
A customizable, 3D-printable ear mold designed to correct newborn outer-ear deformities within 2-6 weeks of birth.
awards.follow_on: Reached 2024 Stella Zhang NVC 2024 NVC semi-finalist + Life Sciences runner-up. Christine Ly graduated UCI BME June 2024 and joined the USC BioMEMS lab as a PhD student in August 2024.

awards.project: A microfluidic chip that mimics brain function for neurological drug testing.
At-home pet fecal testing kits that ship to a partner lab for analysis.
A B2B marketplace for corrugated cardboard pallets that streamlines the pallet procurement process.

years.theme: Wearable Health Sensors and Maternal-Health AI

awards.project: An AI mobile and web app that diagnoses tuberculosis. Users photograph their TB-test injection site with a coin for scale; Azure Cognitive Services calculates risk by measuring skin reaction relative to coin reference.
awards.members_note: Yogita Mallikarjun Pattan and Aditya Sreerama are credited on the Microsoft Imagine Cup team page but were not listed on the BBComp results page
awards.follow_on: Won Microsoft Imagine Cup Epic Challenge 2023 American Region ($5K + $100K grand prize finalist slot); reached Top 3 worldwide at Imagine Cup World Championship 2023 (TAWI from Kenya won the championship)

awards.project: Simplifies the process of finding a restaurant for a group with different tastes and dietary preferences.
A restaurant ranking and marketing platform.
awards.follow_on: Named one of the 10 finalists at the 2023 Stella Zhang NVC (19th annual, first year as the Stella Zhang-branded NVC).

awards.project: A pulse oximeter and continuous blood-pressure monitor integrated into a sleek slipper design for at-home monitoring of pregnant patients to help diagnose preeclampsia early.
A portable, rapid-response EEG aimed at non-convulsive seizures and stroke detection in pre-hospital settings.
Glasses-mounted real-time audio translation and transcription for hearing-impaired and multilingual settings.
An app for pregnant women and new mothers to manage mood - Nourish, Nurture, Nudge.

An electric reusable consumer-grade PPE for protection against airborne substances.
Toroidal aerospike for liquid-fueled rockets - exploits the aerospike's 90% better performance than a bell nozzle.

Startup marketplace and funding platform for youth-led startups, providing online entrepreneurship coaching, a mentor/peer network, and the first rewards-based crowdfunding platform investing in youth-led startups.
awards.follow_on: Caitlyn Yang founded sister venture StartSmart (startsmart.co); was a Blackstone LaunchPad / Techstars top-30 semifinalist (out of 900); joined Wayfinder. Now Mechanical Engineer at SpaceX.

awards.project: Early-stage tech-enabled health and wellness company pairing people with personalized nutrition solutions / food-pairing technology for restaurants.
awards.follow_on: Won 2022 Stella Zhang NVC Business Products & Services 1st ($10,000). Catlin Tran 23 named as winner. Listed in UCI Beall Applied Innovation startup directory.

awards.project: Interactive cybersecurity-learning platform with hands-on labs for proactive secure-code education.
Eye-care startup improving glaucoma management via the TonoLase, an at-home non-invasive intraocular-pressure monitoring device.
awards.follow_on: Lily McGrale was a 2021 Blackstone LaunchPad Fellow and Summer 2021 VentureWell E-Team participant; finalist 2022 TigerLaunch; team also won 2022 Stella Zhang life-sciences track. Effectively the successor to the 2019 AllerChain combined-track finalist team. Lily McGrale is now R&D Engineer II at Medtronic; the TonoLase product did not reach standalone commercialization.

awards.project: Affordable phoropter for low-income communities lacking access to expensive vision-test devices.
AI-powered biomedical device for non-invasive in-home breast-cancer testing.

years.theme: Mobile Health Data and Wearable Cardiology

awards.project: Health data collection using a well-designed mobile app interface to sell consumer blood tests, immunology tests, whole genome sequencing, and mobility assessments.
Mobile-first online giving experience prioritizing modern donors with curated short-form video content from vetted nonprofits.
Two-sided platform allowing travelers to acquire foreign currency from their lodging - bed & breakfast, hostel, or hotel.
Transforming the way blood pressure is measured using soft-skin-like pressure sensors.
awards.follow_on: Now operating as Vena Vitals (founded 2019; Y Combinator-backed). Co-founders: Joshua Kim (CTO; UCI Materials Science PhD 2013-2018 in Khine Lab; UIUC Chemistry BS 2013), Michelle Khine (UCI BME professor and recurring BBComp faculty mentor), Ray Liu (CEO; Harvard MBA + UC Berkeley MS + UIUC BS; previously head of product at two acquired healthtech startups). Total raised: $1.43M; investors include Y Combinator, MedTech Innovator, NSF, Morado Ventures, Founders Inc., HealthTech Arkansas, EvoNexus, plus a Beall Applied Innovation PoP grant. 14 employees, 600+ patients tested in operating rooms. Won 2023 University Lab Partners Pitch.Launch.Grow. Orange County competition (MedTech Track). MARCH 2026: opened new R&D laboratory at the Roseman University of Nevada Summerlin campus, taking lab space inside the new 120,000-square-foot Roseman Bioventures life-science incubator. FDA clearance anticipated within 2026; market launch targeted late 2027 for individuals with hypertension. Future product roadmap: expand the device to monitor heart rate variability and oxygen saturation. Khine Lab PhD alumni on the team: Joshua Kim (Materials Science PhD), Lancy Lin (BME PhD; dissertation 'Conformal Wearable Electronics: Towards Ubiquitous Physiological Monitoring'; lead author of 'Paint-On Epidermal Electronics for On-Demand Sensors and Circuits' Advanced Electronic Materials 2021), Sophia Chou (BME PhD).

awards.project: Improving quality of patient care and outcomes by creating accessible hand-held portable brain monitoring devices. Now operating as CenSyn Inc., a Berkeley SkyDeck-funded company.
awards.follow_on: Founded CenSyn Inc. in 2019 (Ayushi Patel CEO, Andy Bhushan business strategist, Trevor Silence). Product: CenSyn PenEEG. Funding: $105K Seed from Berkeley SkyDeck (Sept 28, 2021); other investors: Arizona Commerce Authority, 1517 Fund, HonorHealth, Monsoon Venture Fund, Skydeck Capital. Executive Chairman: Peter Crosby (40 yrs medical-device industry). Pursuing FDA 510(k) clearance.

awards.project: Utilizes intellectual property developed at UCI's Beckman Laser Institute for a portable blood-flow imaging modality (diabetic foot ulcer monitoring).

awards.project: Mobile application that helps users find their lost items through an immersive AR journey.
awards.follow_on: Zarina Bahadur enrolled in the inaugural class of UCI's Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship (MIE) program at the Paul Merage School and founded 123 Baby Box. In 2020 she won the Stella Zhang NVC Grand Prize ($25K total - Grand Prize plus Consumer Products 1st), the first MIE student ever to win NVC. The company also won a $50K TV pitch contest. April 2023: closed an oversubscribed $1.2M pre-seed round (total raised $1.3M+) led by XRC Labs with participation from Sunstone Fund, Salt Lake City Angels, VC California Crescent, plus angels Mark Friedman (ex-Steve Madden) and Demos Parneros (ex-Barnes & Noble CEO). Targeting Series A metrics of $100K MRR / $1M ARR. Grew 245% in 2024, quadrupled revenue, 14% monthly growth; planning ~$10M next round over 18-20 months; signed a distributor deal to ship to 1M customers via a top breast-pump distributor. Ting-Wei Lin is now UX Designer at Cathay Financial Holding (Taiwan).

awards.project: Cross-platform AR/VR application for creative teams in entertainment to view, communicate, and collaborate during design and production.
Web application as a centralized political-information hub allowing users to compare their stances with elected representatives and candidates.
Flapping Wing Manned Aerial Vehicle (FWMAV) - non-invasive drone replacing each of four traditional propellers of a quadcopter with a pair of mechanical wings.
Re-engineered syringe that eliminates the need for old syringe priming methods, resolving medical errors brought about by outdated technology.
awards.follow_on: Officially formed as a Delaware C corporation on February 9, 2018; 100% owned by undergraduates at UCI and San Diego State University. CEO and principal inventor: Bien Gutierrez (UCI BME senior; inspired by his experience caring for his diabetic grandfather as a teenager). Wendy Nguyen handles logistics and operations. Won 2nd place + $750 in the Elevator Pitch category at TCU's 2018 Values and Ventures Competition. Site: humbletech.uci.design.

awards.project: Customized braces alleviating obstacles faced by orthodontists; halves treatment time.
awards.members_note: Awards roster credits Mardy and Abbaspour; combined-track registration also lists Wratten and Roein-Peikar
awards.follow_on: Same year (2018): also won Stella Zhang NVC Life Sciences 1st place. Now operating as BRIUS Technologies (rebrand). HQ: Carrollton, TX. Founded 2016 (predates the BBComp placement by 2 years; Mechanodontics was the team-name used for the BBComp). $46.2M total raised across 19 investors including a $19.5M Series B led by View Ventures (May 6, 2025) with Sonder Capital, Invus, SUM Ventures, Tech Wildcatters, Cheyenne Partners, GT Healthcare Capital Partners, plus institutional investors SeedFolio, Startup UCLA, QB3. CEO: Lea Ellermeier. Product: the Brava Independent Mover CAD/CAM orthodontic system - moves teeth independently and autonomously, reducing overall treatment time by half and cutting visits from 25 to 3. Co-founder Mehdi Peikar holds a PhD in Biomechanics from Johns Hopkins, MS in Quantum Mechanics and Condensed Matter from UIUC, second-round three-year orthodontics residency at UCLA in 2019, DDS from UCLA School of Dentistry. Now Founder, CTO, and CMO of Brius Technologies. Won the 2017 UCLA School of Law Lowell Milken Institute-Sandler Prize ($70K) and the 2019 UIUC Cozad NVC ($25K Grand Prize) - the first BBComp-traceable team to win a major out-of-state university competition. HIGHEST-FUNDED BBComp-traceable venture on record.

awards.project: Collaborative photo-sharing platform that streamlines categorization by allowing users to upload photos to communal albums tied to specific locations.

Motion Analytic System (AirTouch) - wearable hand computer with haptic feedback for note-taking and gesture input. Originally an interactive glove for visually impaired students learning piano/woodwind, inspired by a music instructor's method of tapping fingers to indicate notes.
awards.follow_on: Evolved into Palmplug Inc., an active Pacific Northwest startup focused on Spatial Computing, Wearables, Health, Robotics, and AI. Palmplug's wearable delivers hand-and-finger tracking with 13ms latency, combining hand tracking, haptic feedback, and visual cues. Targets robotics, VR/AR, healthcare, and sports. Founder & CEO: Olaoluwa Adesanya (UCI CS BS 2015-2017), who is also at Microsoft (post-UCI).

awards.project: AI-powered 'on-demand anything' task-fulfillment marketplace.
awards.follow_on: Co-founders Karan Kanwar and Martin Gomez incorporated Wing AI Technologies (commonly Wing Assistant) in 2018; the Wing team won the 2018 Stella Zhang NVC Consumer Services 1st place ($10K). Wing is a cloud-based contract-workforce platform for virtual assistants powered by AI plus real human operators. Scaled to 1,000+ employees in 10 countries across 4 continents. UC Berkeley SkyDeck Spring 2020 cohort. Institutional investors: Berkeley SkyDeck and Troy Labs (per Crunchbase/Tracxn). Kausthub Raj Jadhav is now Product Engineering Manager at LILA Games (Bangalore); previously ContractKen, Loop, Pathrise, Meta Platforms, Varsity Tutors, Wing Assistant, BeWo Technologies. He also co-founded SoCal's largest AI non-profit, AI@UCI.
awards.company_name: Wing AI Technologies (Wing Assistant) - founder follow-on

awards.project: Affordable competitive prosthetic hand designed to outperform existing low-cost options.
Accessible low-cost tools for motivational walking-rehab.
awards.follow_on: See 2016 Red Lion Robotics entry; this is the same team returning in 2017 with Hwan Heo replacing Brandon Tsuge - the only confirmed back-to-back Beall 2nd-place team in the joint era. Same active company (Red Lion Robotics, product GRAM wheelchair attachment).

awards.project: Affordable point-of-care therapeutic for diabetic foot ulcers.
awards.follow_on: Active commercial company at University Lab Partners (UCI Research Park). Founded 2016 (Syntrfuge concept conceived during senior-year class in 2015). Funding: $10M raise announced March 2023; $2.2M seed (Aug 2021); $300K Phase I SBIR/NIH grant (Oct 2017). Product: Syntrfuge - the world's first and only Automated Microfat Processing System (per company marketing). FDA-cleared per the company site. Single-use disposable medical device that processes fat in under 10 minutes; targets facial fat loss, knee osteoarthritis, and diabetic foot ulcers. Co-founders: Ahmed Zobi (CEO, EMBA, 8+ years in microfluidics/biomechanics; April 2025 speaker at Sunstone Management grant workshop), Hugo Salas (VP Business Development, UCI BME B.S. with micro/nano specialization + Business Management minor), Justin Stovner (VP Engineering, UCI BME B.S. and M.S. Class of 2016 specializing in additive/subtractive manufacturing; lead engineer of the SyntrFuge System).

years.theme: The Internet of Things and Bluetooth Low Energy

awards.project: Virtual Reality Therapy Experience for people with Autism Spectrum Disorder so they can learn and practice social skills.
Uses smartphone/smartwatch sensors to play the right music at the right time.
Mobile platform inviting college students to dine in homes, order takeout, share stories and enjoy authentic homemade cuisine.
Tag - a small Bluetooth Low Energy device used with a smartphone for tracking belongings and sending distress signals; leverages a crowd-GPS network. Predates Apple AirTag by ~5 years.
Accessible tools for physical rehabilitation and assistance.
awards.follow_on: Active company. Product: GRAM (Gait Rehab Adaptive Machine) - a low-cost wheelchair attachment that provides motivational mobility and therapy for patients healing from walking disability. Named in honor of Yasemin Sarigul-Klijn's grandmother (whose immobility inspired the project). Yasemin Sarigul-Klijn is Founder; UCI BME PhD student in rehab robotics. Won the 2017 Aging 2.0 Orange County regional business competition and advanced to the national competition. Same team returned in 2017 (Beall 2nd, the only confirmed back-to-back placement of any team in the joint era; Hwan Heo replaced Brandon Tsuge). Peter L. Wang served as Lead Design Engineer (Oct 2015 - Oct 2017); UCI PhD 2018 in robot kinematics; now Research Staff Scientist at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the Disruptive Manufacturing Systems Development Group. Brandon Tsuge is now Lecturer in UCI's Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering with a Doctor of Engineering and PE license; published research on linkage systems for gait-cycle rehabilitation robotics; also at Zymo Research Corp.

awards.project: Rapid quantitative diagnostic test for bloodstream infections and antibiotic resistance.
awards.follow_on: Same year (2016): team also won 2nd place + $5,000 at the UCI Business Plan Competition Life Sciences/Clean Tech track and participated in the UCI BioAccel Solutions Challenge med-tech start-up program. CeleriBio itself did not commercialize. Team lead Louai Labanieh went on to a Stanford PhD (Crystal Mackall Lab + Parker Scholar) in synthetic biology and protein engineering for CAR-T cells (drug-regulated switches and logic-gated protein circuits). In 2021 he co-founded CARGO Therapeutics with Crystal Mackall, Nancy Goodman, and Robbie Majzner; his technologies were licensed to CARGO and supported a Phase I clinical trial of the SNIP CAR platform in relapsed/refractory solid cancers at Stanford. CARGO Therapeutics agreed to be acquired by Concentra Biosciences on July 8, 2025 at $4.379/share cash + CVR (~$170.7M total per InsideArbitrage analyst calculation (the GlobeNewswire press release states only $4.379/share cash + CVR, not an aggregate)); acquisition tender offer closed August 18, 2025; merger completed August 19, 2025; delisted from Nasdaq. This is the FIRST DOCUMENTED BBComp-traceable M&A exit. Labanieh is now Assistant Professor at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. Other team members: Sadaf Mirnia is now Senior Supplier Quality Engineer at Medtronic.

notable_finalist_followons.follow_on: First on-demand pickup service that rewards users for recycling at home. Founded May 2015 (predating the BBComp placement by ~1 year). Commercial team: Arthur Avetisov (CEO and Co-Founder, UCI Political Science and Economics '15), Brian Leung (COO and Co-Founder, UCI International Studies '16), Malik Ahmad (Co-Founder and CMO). Leung and Avetisov met through UCI's Delta Sigma Pi business fraternity. Funding: $240K from MuckerLab (Santa Monica; also accepted into the 2017 cohort) + $20K from Dorm Room Fund = $260K+ total raised; last seed round closed December 28, 2016. Won the 2015 ANTrepreneur of the Year Award from the ANTrepreneur Center (then Blackstone LaunchPad).

First documented BBComp-traceable M&A exit: CARGO Therapeutics (co-founded by 2016 CeleriBio Beall 3rd lead Louai Labanieh) acquired by Concentra Biosciences for $4.379/share + CVR (~$170.7M total). Signed July 8, 2025; tender offer closed August 18, 2025; merger completed August 19, 2025; delisted from Nasdaq.
Vena Vitals (2019 Beall 1st Qardiac follow-on) opens R&D lab at Roseman University of Nevada Summerlin (March 2026;); FDA clearance anticipated within 2026; market launch targeted late 2027
Sentinel (2024 Butterworth 1st) publicly launched as Spotter AI's flagship hiring/screening/compliance platform on February 17, 2026; March 31, 2026 expansion adds digital driver application

data_integrity_flags.description: The bbcomp.tech.uci.edu past/2014 and past/2015 pages render duplicate content (both showing 2015 winners). The 2014 placements are corroborated independently via the Samueli press release; the 2015 placements are now verified as correct content (the 2014 page is the incorrect duplicate).

The legacy archive-www.ics.uci.edu/community/news/view_news endpoints currently return HTTP 500 for the relevant article IDs (541, 550); content was recovered via cached web search and the live ics.uci.edu/archive-news/ redirector. Content for 2012 and 2013 is now fully verified.

The competition ran in 2010 (7th annual) and 2011 (8th annual) but no public records of winners surfaced during research, despite direct fetches against the live ICS news system and the legacy archive subdomain. Contributions welcome.

An earlier note in this archive claimed Donny 'Don' Magnuson was on the 2017 Stella Zhang NVC Grand Prize Winner team Purist (UCI radioisotope startup). Re-verification against the official UCI Beall Applied Innovation Purist profile (innovation.uci.edu/2018/05/purist-cooking-up-radioisotopes-that-can-save-lives/) names only Leila Safavi-Tehrani (Co-founder/Lead) and Mikael Nilsson (UCI Professor of Chemical Engineering and Materials Science, Co-founder). The Magnuson-on-Purist claim is therefore flagged as UNVERIFIED pending a primary source. Magnuson's COMPAS-team participation at the 2017 NVC (2nd place, Consumer Services) is verified separately.

VeinGuard has a project-site roster that exceeds the official BBComp roster. The official BBComp 2025 winners page lists 5 members; the project site at veinguard.uci.design lists 7 (additionally Raveena Atwal and Marlena Ramanis). Vision Board previously retained a 4th name (Phillip Peterson) from prior research; this was removed in May 2026 after verification against the official BBComp page found no match.
